The root cause is not casing and not street suffixes — it is that
address strings are not a stable key across NEI editions
is (95.4% name-stable 2019→2022, §05). Any address-derived key silently manufactures departures whenever a publisher restyles an address.
True industrial departure counts are 15 (2019 baseline) to 33 (2017 baseline), not 68.
Fix for the plan: key on
; use normalized address only as a secondary corroborator; and assert as a regression test that no emitted departure names a business whose
appears in any later edition. Hopkins Steel Works (id 8130) is the named test case.

The normalizer successfully unifies the schema across four editions by lowercasing keys and stripping underscores. Pairwise intersection sizes (11,014–11,895) all exceed the 5,000-record threshold asserted by the tests, confirming normalization is working and demonstrating why this is necessary: without lowercasing the

drift, cross-year comparison would silently return zero matches. This silent zero was the failure mode that caught the departures defect in §14: a publisher's field-name restyle creates apparent departures if the key is not normalized. The loader now provides a stable key for all downstream analysis. Hopkins Steel Works is confirmed as the regression test case: it is present in all four editions and must remain so as departures analysis is built.

This is corroboration, not circular: §14's per-baseline counts were computed independently, before

The old layer's 68 claimed departures are cut to 34, a reduction of exactly half. Every one of those 34 has been checked, at generation time, against every edition after its own baseline (that is what

computes and what the regression test verifies) — none of them can be Hopkins-style false positives. This does not certify that the 34 are true departures in every clerical sense (e.g. a business could have relocated within the same municipality and re-registered under a new
, which this method cannot distinguish from a genuine closure) — that limitation is inherent to the NEI data model, not to this fix, and is unchanged from before.
